summary.headline: Health X Platform Q2 FY27 revenue rose 59% YoY to Rs 489 CR, with gross margin at 8.3% and operating cost ratio down to 10.8% of revenue.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations reached Rs 489 CR, up 59% YoY and 11% QoQ, with the B2B Retailer Shakti platform contributing Rs 429 CR. Gross margin widened to 8.3% of revenue (from 7.5% a year ago), and total opex fell to 10.8% of revenue (from 12.4%), narrowing EBITDA loss to 3.5% of revenue. Management said EBITDA was broadly flat sequentially as a percentage of revenue, with employee cost rising to Rs 31 CR on new market hiring. Management also launched the Retail Air retailer billing app and reiterated a long-term 30% CAGR target and a 10% gross margin ambition by about FY29.

segments.name: Retailer Shakti (B2B)
segments.commentary: Rs 429 CR in Q2, up 60% YoY and 18% QoQ; the largest segment and the main driver of group revenue growth. Serves roughly 80,000 retail pharmacies per management.

segments.name: Satsang Sundar (B2C)
segments.commentary: Rs 55 CR in Q2, up 39% YoY; management says it has grown for six consecutive quarters since full control was regained. Health Buddy franchise model delivers last mile.

segments.name: Jito private label
segments.commentary: Cumulative sales Rs 2.2 CR at about 60% gross margin; 52 franchise outlets live with 81 in pipeline. Management targets Rs 6-10 CR next quarter, but cautioned the base is very small.

segments.name: Diagnostics
segments.commentary: Revenue of about Rs 0.8 CR in Q2, immaterial to group.

guidance_outlook: Management targets around 30% compounded revenue growth, versus Indian pharma market growth of about 12% (IPM); it said the company should be modelled at about 30%.
Gross margin path: 8-9% in FY27 (8.5-8.6% cited), 9-10% in FY28, and 10-11% in FY29, with 50-100 bps annual expansion described as achievable.
Opex reduction targeted at about 2% through scale; management said EBITDA will recover over time.

Revised Jito model: 13% of revenue from Jito-branded medicine in FY29; FY29 revenue target cut to Rs 4,000 CR (from Rs 6,000 CR), with Retailer Shakti Rs 2,000 CR to about Rs 900 CR, and EBITDA guided at 5-6% (vs earlier ~5%).
Merger with the listed entity: SEBI observation expected by end-December 2026; NCLT filing thereafter, with completion estimated around June 2027 or earlier.
Incremental fulfilment capacity of about 5.95 lakh sq ft in pipeline; incremental investment payback 3-4 years.
capex_capacity: West Bengal fulfilment centre fully automated and sized for about 18 months of projected growth; Noida warehouse moved to a larger site with double capacity, covering 3-4 years.
Goa warehouse upgraded, sized for about 3 years of growth.

Under construction or planned: West Bengal 1.2 lakh sq ft; Goa 75,000 sq ft; Lucknow 80,000 sq ft; Udaipur 80,000 sq ft (phase 1 of 20,000 sq ft, then 1.2 lakh sq ft); Bhubaneswar 20,000 sq ft phase 1, then 1.2 lakh sq ft. Total additional capacity about 5.95 lakh sq ft.
Three smaller 20,000 sq ft warehouses (Ranchi, Patna, Bhubaneswar) being signed up, about six months before operation; larger Udaipur warehouse expected in about 18 months.

Investment in Q2 cited as Rs 7 CR for Noida; a Kolkata warehouse upgrade in progress. Management said total investment outflow was about Rs 70 CR lower in H1 and attributed it to ongoing fulfilment capex.
demand_pricing: Management said 90% of orders are delivered within 24 hours; over 76% of customers and 66% of retailers are from tier 2 and tier 3 India.
More than 90% of purchases come directly from pharma companies through enterprise channels, per management.
Retail Air (mobile-first retailer billing and inventory app, launched on Google Play) is live; management said retailers are billing on it. Adoption data to be shared next quarter.
Retailer credit: management said the company has partnered with two national banks and some NBFCs for retailer working capital, but bank adoption is slow.
Competition: management said online platforms serve chronic medicine, while acute medicine is served by local pharmacies, which Satsang Sundar and Retailer Shakti also serve.

qa_highlights.question: What are the advantages of large distributors versus small ones in margin, delivery cost and fill-rate terms?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited three advantages for scale: bulk purchase discounts from suppliers, lower operating cost per unit processed, and diversification across markets. It did not quantify the margin gap and said no industry study exists.

qa_highlights.question: Why will customers wait for online delivery when faster options exist?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said online platforms serve chronic medicine, while acute needs go to nearby pharmacies. It cited trust and barcode traceability against counterfeits, and pricing advantage for planned monthly refills.

qa_highlights.question: How is Jito brand performing, and what is the path to 10% gross margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Jito cumulative sales were Rs 2.2 CR at about 60% gross margin; management expects Rs 6-10 CR next quarter. Gross margin path is 8-9% in FY27, 9-10% in FY28, and 10-11% in FY29, and management stressed this is a target, not guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity and incremental cost of fulfilment expansion, and what are the gross margin levers?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity additions total about 5.95 lakh sq ft. Management said incremental cost is about 27-28% of incremental EBITDA, recovered in 3-4 years, and cited Jito, volume, data monetisation, and logistics as margin levers, with data monetisation around 1% of gross margin.

qa_highlights.question: Is 30% growth conservative, and how will cost grow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 growth was about 20%, averaging about 33% over the period, and it is targeting about 30% CAGR. Opex is expected to fall as a percentage of revenue as scale builds; new-market hiring drove employee cost higher.

qa_highlights.question: How is cash being used, and what is the status of the merger?
qa_highlights.answer: Treasury is held pending merger completion, as the treasury company's shareholders have not agreed to a buyback. The SEBI observation is expected by end-December 2026, with NCLT filing afterwards and completion around mid-2027.

risks_watch: EBITDA is still negative at -3.5% of revenue; sequential EBITDA margin was flat, and management said further new-market hiring is ongoing.
Jito revenue mix shift lowers FY29 revenue target to Rs 4,000 CR from Rs 6,000 CR, a sizeable cut that management attributes to lower pricing (about one-third of branded prices).
Merger timing depends on SEBI observation expected by December 2026 and NCLT approval, which typically takes 4-6 months.

Treasury deployment: management declined to put idle cash into receivable investments that would add about Rs 50 CR a year of income, so reported profit depends on the company's stated accounting choices.
Retailer Air adoption and the bank/NBFC credit partnerships are early-stage; management said bank adoption is slow.
Management's disclosure of incremental fulfilment costs is limited, as costs are centralised across warehouses.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on long-term strategy and platform ownership, but guarded on near-term profitability and on specific margin and cost numbers, which it repeatedly framed as targets rather than guidance. Answers to analyst questions on cost breakdowns and Jito economics were partly evasive, with several figures labelled as rough estimates.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Gross margin at 8.3% in Q2 FY27 (up 80 bps YoY, 40 bps QoQ) with management guiding 8-9% in FY27, 9-10% in FY28 and 10-11% in FY29, and 50-100 bps annual expansion; but EBITDA still -3.5% of revenue and opex cut only about 2% through scale.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: About 5.95 lakh sq ft of fulfilment capacity is under construction or planned (West Bengal 1.2 lakh, Lucknow 80k, Udaipur 80k, Goa 75k), and three 20k sq ft warehouses (Ranchi, Patna, Bhubaneswar) are being signed about six months before operation.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management targets about 30% CAGR against IPM growth of about 12%; Q2 revenue grew 59% YoY and Retailer Shakti grew 60% YoY to Rs 429 CR, with Jito expected at Rs 6-10 CR next quarter from a Rs 2.2 CR cumulative base.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is already rising (Rs 7 CR Noida, Kolkata upgrade in progress) and about 5.95 lakh sq ft is in the pipeline with 3-4 year payback, though management said H1 total investment outflow was about Rs 70 CR lower, so the pace is uncertain.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY29 revenue target was cut to Rs 4,000 CR from Rs 6,000 CR and EBITDA guidance was only nudged to 5-6%, while management framed margin figures as targets rather than guidance.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: EBITDA is still -3.5% of revenue, opex is rising with new-market hiring (employee cost Rs 31 CR vs Rs 27.7 CR in Q1), and the FY29 revenue target was already cut by about one-third.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Jito private label has 52 outlets live with 81 in pipeline and an FY29 target of 13% of revenue from Jito-branded medicine; the Retail Air app is live with adoption data due next quarter, and an AI consumer app is targeted around October next year.

rows.label: Net working capital down to 23 days from 28
rows.why: NWC fell to 23 days (6% of revenue) from 28 days in the June quarter, with inventory at 35 days and payables at 13 days, though bank credit partnerships are early-stage and bank adoption is slow.

rows.label: Merger with listed entity; SEBI observation by end-December 2026
rows.why: SEBI observation is expected by end-December 2026, then NCLT filing with completion estimated around June 2027, though NCLT approval typically takes 4-6 months and treasury cash is held pending merger completion.

rows.label: Jito branded medicine pricing and FY29 revenue cut
rows.why: FY29 revenue target cut to Rs 4,000 CR from Rs 6,000 CR, with Retailer Shakti cut to about Rs 900 CR from Rs 2,000 CR, as Jito pricing is about one-third of branded prices.

tone.note: Management was confident on the long-term 30% growth, capacity build and platform ownership, but cautious on near-term profitability and framed margin and cost numbers as targets; analysts pressed on cost breakdowns, Jito economics and the cut to the FY29 revenue target.

quality.why: Revenue grew 59% YoY to Rs 489 CR, led by Retailer Shakti B2B (Rs 429 CR, +60% YoY, +18% QoQ) with Satsang Sundar +39% YoY, and the brief cites no one-off gains, low base, acquisition or exclusion-based growth figures in this quarter; the merger is still pending, so no consolidation is in the reported growth.
